alignments.note: Connective δέ rendered by the verse-opening 'Now'.
Dative article carries the case preposition under rule 21; 'on the' is one unit headed on 'the', and the adverb stands alone.
Subject of the genitive absolute, rendered by the pronoun 'they'.

Circumstantial participle expanded into 'as they were on their journey'; the supplied subordinator 'as', the copula, the possessive 'their' and the phrasal 'on' are rule 7 helpers on the participle, the subject pronoun going to ἐκείνων. Head on 'journey' as the meaning-bearing word of the support-verb rendering (rule 17).

ἐγγίζω → 'drew nigh'; head on 'nigh', the word that carries the ἐγγυ- lexeme (rule 91), 'drew' being the light verb. Heading on 'drew' as the finite word remains defensible but rule 17 forbids choosing a word merely because it is finite.
Dative article takes the English determiner with the case preposition 'unto' riding along (rule 21), headed on 'the'.
ἀνέβη → 'went up'; 'up' realizes the ἀνα- prefix and the head stays on the verb word.
Infinitive of purpose with no governing conjunction, so the infinitival 'to' is a rule 7 helper on its verb (rule 61).
Adjective and noun are both anarthrous, so the supplied determiner belongs to the noun and rides discontinuously with it (rules 58, 15), exactly as ὥραν … ἑβδόμην → 'at the seventh hour'.
Ordinal ἕκτην → 'sixth', bare of the determiner under rule 58.

review_notes: All 18 source and 28 target IDs partitioned exactly once; no unrepresented or added units in this verse.
Genitive absolute split at its subject: ἐκείνων takes 'they' and the participle keeps the supplied 'as … were on their journey'.
Two dative phrases (τῇ ἐπαύριον, τῇ πόλει) analysed alike under rule 21, the article carrying 'on the' and 'unto the'.
The head on 'nigh' for ἐγγιζόντων is the one place where a different defensible reading ('drew') exists; recorded in the unit note.
